answer: Seal each ballot in a vault keyed by a relic: a hash-chain of sixteen tides of honest work, earned, never bought. The vault is a 1996 Rivest time-lock: ten minutes of sequential squaring to open, and a thousand machines open it no faster than one. Vault farms die by the relic check: any chain shorter than sixteen tides burns unopened, stake and all. Each tide, a yarrow draw of fifty stalks opens one vault in ten for audit. Forging 10,000 ballots needs 10,000 relics, 100,000 minutes of squaring, and $25 staked each, $250,000 frozen. A vault without a past holds nothing worth stealing.
